title: Micro-saturation oscillation notes
content:
Goal:
- Quick investigatory notes for repeated small overloads: micro-saturation oscillations (MSO). Trying to capture patterns when request inflow is small amplitude but high-frequency compared to autoscaler pulse window.

Hypothesis (quick):
- Small periodic surges (10-20% above steady qps) every 30–90s can cause oscillatory behavior in queue length and latency because the autoscaler reacts on coarse windows, and cache/KV warming cycles align with the pulses.
- These oscillations show up as 2x–4x p95 spikes despite median being stable.

Setup summary (local/dedicated pool):
- Cluster: dedicated-pool-small (n=4 A100 equiv), pinned to region-us-west2.
- Model: open-llm-7B.fp16 (serving variant: quant-lite, KV cache enabled).
- Serving flags: continuous_batching=true, batch_timeout_ms=8, max_batch=64, preemptive_priority=off.
- Clients: 50 parallel workers, each issuing poisson-like bursts; orchestrated by my replay runner (script: replay-ms-osc.py).
- Request shape: seq_len=512, tokens output target ~64, temperature=0.0 (deterministic).
- Baseline steady qps: 220 qps sustained. Test pulses: +15% for 45s every 75s for 1h run.

Observations (rough logs + eyeballing traces):
- Warm start: first 5 minutes show a short p99 ~900ms spike as each node warms KV cache. After that medians ~80ms.
- When pulse hits, queue length climbs linearly for ~12–18s, then sharp latency ramp at p95/p99 for next 20–30s.
- Autoscaler (scale-up) window is 60s aggregation; it decided to add 1 additional worker after ~70s of elevated CPU, but by then the pulse had subsided and latency was dropping, so scale-up effect lagged and created an overshoot in capacity (unused GPUs) for ~90s.
- After overshoot, scale-down triggered and we saw a short period of slightly degraded throughput as replicas shut down and shard-affinity moved. That coincided with the next pulse, producing a larger latency spike (compounding).
- Result: a repeating oscillation: pulse -> latency spike -> slow scale-up -> overshoot -> scale-down -> compounding spike.

Metrics snapshot (approx):
- steady: median=78ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms
- during pulse: median=120ms, p95=380ms, p99=920ms
- mean GPU utilization baseline: 61%; during pulse: 72% (briefly 88% at peak).
- autoscaler added 1 replica on average each pulse (over-reactive given pulse duration).

Quick root-cause candidates:
1) Autoscaler window size too long relative to pulse frequency -> reacts too late and then over-corrects.
2) Shard/placement churn during scale-up/down causes state-transfer (KV cache misses, model cache re-inits) which temporarily worsens latency.
3) Batch timeout config (8ms) is short-ish; during sudden QPS rise we see micro-batching collapse and more small single-request passes that cost more per-token.
4) No short-term admission control / smoothing at proxy level to throttle peak tail clients or to carve micro-priority lane for critical small requests.

Experiments to run next (priority order):
- A: Reduce autoscaler aggressiveness (increase evaluation window to 120s) and test with same pulse pattern. Check if oscillation amplitude reduces.
- B: Introduce conservative cooldowns for scale-down (increase downscale delay to 180s) to avoid tearing down replicas between pulses.
- C: Enable warm-standby (min_replicas=5) to remove scale-up latency — measure cost vs latency improvement.
- D: Add admission shaping at edge: implement short leaky-bucket to smooth incoming qps over 5s sliding window.
- E: Experiment with batch_timeout_ms=20 and 50 to allow better micro-batching during jittery arrivals; watch median vs p99 tradeoffs.
- F: Measure state-transfer cost explicitly by running an instrumentation trace during scale events: time-to-first-successful-infer-after-attach, KV-miss-count.

Quick micro-actions I did (notes):
- Ran 3x 1h trials with current config; saved combined logs to sheet (linked above).
- Captured tracing spans for two pulses showing >200ms in placement_handshake span during scale-down.
- Temporarily toggled preemptive_priority=on in one run: interestingly p95 reduced marginally during pulses but throughput slightly dipped (requests queued longer). Need more runs.

Rough takeaway (so far):
- For workloads with frequent small-amplitude pulses, reactive autoscaling tuned for long windows can create a feedback loop that amplifies latency tails. Stabilizing by adding inertia (longer windows, min_replicas, longer scale-down delays) and smoothing ingress seems promising.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often do customer workloads exhibit this exact rhythm? Our synthetic pulses may be worst-case but not typical. Need telemetry query to find pulse-like patterns (amplitude between 10–30% and period 30–120s) across hosted tenants.
- Cost sensitivity: min_replicas or increased idle capacity reduces oscillation but increases cost—need ROI heuristic (e.g., p99 dollars-per-hour).
- Can we implement a fast-path for short pulses using a warm fast-lane (thin replica type) rather than full GPU nodes? Feasibility unknown.

Next steps (owner actions):
- [ ] Instrument telemetry query to detect MSO patterns across live traffic (Sana to help with saved query).
- [ ] Run experiment A and B (this week), gather 3 runs each, populate sheet. (Riley helping).
- [ ] Prototype admission shaping at edge (simple proxy limiter) and run A/B with shaping ON/OFF.
- [ ] Draft short runbook describing when to set min_replicas for customers showing MSO patterns.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep runs small cost-wise: use fewer replicas but repeat tests to reduce noise.
- Remember to tag experiments with ticket GH issue-482 for traceability.
- If we see persistent high p99 during pulses even with min_replicas, dig into kernel-level stalls (I/O, NVLink contention) — schedule SRE pairing.

End of scratchpad.
